notes: Active means issued on or before 1 Nov 2026 and expiring after it. Over 2022-2026 the monthly count of shed jobs ran 9,500-10,600 and NB jobs 3,100-4,200 (data/derived/construction/active_by_month.csv). On the date, 59,249 distinct DOB NOW jobs held at least one active permit, of which 2,712 were new buildings; the rest are alterations. Construction fences (6,947), supported scaffolds (3,587) and suspended scaffolds (3,096) add to what is visible from the street. A wider NB definition (first permit in the last six years and no CO) gives 3,847 jobs, which leaves the ratio near 2. Graph evidence check (12 Nov 2026, after the coordinator's audit): association aFGrNWb1i5 (vacant housing demolitions and 'change in crime', PMID 36228876), cited in the registration, is NOT in the Dataverse v2.1 CSV. The abstract (Kvik et al., Prev Med 2022) shows it is mis-extracted: the -0.068 (95% CI -0.119 to -0.018) is the change in total emergency-department visits per 1,000 people, and demolitions showed no significant change in crime. It should be dropped; it bore on context only, not on any test here. Of the other graph rows cited, UXzKbLS899 (population growth and construction land, Chongqing) is in the CSV. The vacant-lot and renovation rows looked at during the search (3rfxckzPtm, R0ctB4TYK1, CVCABCQUUe, 168lUaKwYN, 20AOg9kwfR, IfVJnDqqH0) are not in the CSV. The graph holds no finding on permits, permit-to-completion ratios, lags or permit lapse, so the research side of every construction claim comes from the literature.
